# Database contract

The service owns its PostgreSQL schema. Other services must use HTTP/events and must not query these tables.

## `personal_teacher`

- `id`: internal UUID primary key;
- `student_id`: opaque external student identifier, unique;
- teacher profile and behavior setting columns;
- `version`: optimistic concurrency version starting at `1`;
- UTC creation and update timestamps.

The table contains no student learning state and has no cross-database foreign keys.

## `personal_teacher_soul`

Stores exactly one soul per `(personal_teacher_id, student_id)` with an
independent optimistic `version`. The composite foreign key guarantees that a
soul cannot be attached to another student's teacher. Fields are limited to
display name, persona code, voice, relationship, and evidence-based
encouragement styles. Mastery, learning paths, attempts, evidence, dialog
history, prompts, and raw events are forbidden. Migration `006` backfills one
default but independently mutable row for every existing PersonalTeacher.

## `teacher_decision`

Stores the immutable pedagogical decision trace: teaching mode, context reference, optional `learning_action_id`, selected pedagogy method/version/stage, strategy, selected action, optional hint level, reason code/summary, policy version, correlation/causation IDs, and timestamp. New lesson-task, practice-task, and project decisions require `learning_action_id` and use it as `correlation_id`. Legacy task rows without an action link remain readable but cannot be attributed during finalization. Migration `007` identifies legacy decisions explicitly and makes every new replaceable method auditable. `reason_summary` is a concise business explanation; raw model reasoning, prompts, student code, and dialog history are forbidden.

## `teacher_outbox`

Stores the complete versioned event envelope until a JetStream acknowledgement is received. Relay replicas claim rows with a bounded lease and `SKIP LOCKED`. Failed publication releases the lease and schedules exponential retry; successful publication records `published_at`. Rows are not deleted by the relay, preserving an operational audit trail.

## `teacher_learning_action_assistance`

Stores exactly one immutable teacher-owned summary per `(student_id, learning_action_id)`: guided/independent context, hint aggregate, intervention flag, up to 300 provider-neutral target observations, and policy version. `correlation_id` equals `learning_action_id`; `causation_id` identifies the student closure event. The row does not contain task outcome, score, confidence, or mastery.

## `teacher_integration_inbox`

Stores one immutable processed marker per source `event_id` and enforces one closure per `(student_id, learning_action_id)`. Finalization inserts this marker, the optional assistance row, and the optional `teacher.assistance.observed` outbox envelope in one transaction. Targetless actions intentionally commit only the inbox marker.

## `teacher_dialog_job`

Stores one durable orchestration record per `dialog.teacher.requested.event_id` and enforces one request per `(dialog_id, source_message_id)`. It preserves Dialog's v2 causation separately from the Teacher-job causation derived from `event_id`, and contains request identities, status, fenced lease metadata, retry timing, optional decision/delivery IDs, and a bounded error code. It never contains Student context, Dialog history, prompt variables, rendered prompts, raw provider responses, or chain-of-thought.

The lifecycle is `queued -> processing -> delivery_pending -> delivered`, with
`completed` for proof-backed `failed_no_effect` and `blocked` for permanent or
reconciliation work. Migration `017` adds nullable v2 dense-turn identities, a
unique `(dialog_id, teacher_turn_sequence)` fence, and
`teacher_dialog_turn_cursor`, `teacher_dialog_turn_proof`, and
`teacher_dialog_turn_outcome`. v2 jobs are claimable only at the cursor's next
sequence when dense ordering is enabled; v1 keeps its legacy claim path.
Delivery or proof-backed no-effect and cursor advancement commit atomically;
retry, lease expiry, `unknown`, `partial`, and `committed_unreconciled` never
advance the cursor. The parsed response body remains private transient delivery
state and is cleared only after verified idempotent Dialog append.

Migration `025` permits a private response to remain on a `blocked` job only
when it was already generated for legacy `practice_task|project`, has a decision
and a positive attempt count, and has no delivered-message identity or delivery
time. The original 48,000-byte UTF-8 limit remains; retained text is also limited
to 12,000 characters. `Block` and reconciliation preserve that exact pending
body without changing claimability, attempts, ordering, or operator policy.
Coordinator and other context behavior stays unchanged. A known committed
Dialog append, including `committed_unreconciled` with a delivery identity,
clears the body. Migration rollback locks the table and fails closed if any
blocked body remains; it never deletes a pending response to restore the old
constraint. An unused/drained install can restore the previous constraint and
apply `025` again.

The proof table stores a durable Student no-effect reference. The outcome table
stores the recoverable terminal result and its distinct turn correlation; it
does not repurpose `TeacherDecision.correlation_id`. The job's proof/outcome
UUIDs are foreign keys, so arbitrary identities cannot satisfy
`failed_no_effect`.

## `teacher_intervention_inbox`

Stores one processed record per `learning.activity.interesting.event_id`. Its
bounded state is the signal type, selected `intervene`/`stay_silent` action,
offer text when applicable, and optional committed Dialog delivery identity.
The row links the same student and PersonalTeacher through a composite foreign
key. A partial unique index permits at most one proactive offer per student and
analytics session; redelivery uses the source event ID as the Dialog
idempotency key. Raw analytics, error text/fingerprints, code, mastery, and
dialog history are never persisted here.

## Telegram channel tables

`teacher_telegram_link_code` stores a 32-byte SHA-256 digest, the exact
student/PersonalTeacher/general-Dialog binding, expiry, and bounded consumption
evidence. Plaintext codes and bot secrets are never persisted.

`teacher_telegram_binding` has `student_id` as its primary key and independent
unique constraints on the numeric Telegram user and private chat identifiers.
Re-linking the same authenticated student replaces only that student's binding;
one Telegram identity cannot be assigned to two students.

`teacher_telegram_delivery` is keyed by the source Dialog message UUID. It
stores only the target chat, pending response body, finite lease/retry state,
and acknowledged Telegram message ID. It is not a conversation history and is
terminal after `sent` or `blocked`.

## `teacher_course_plan_notification_inbox`

Stores one immutable terminal Learning Planner outcome per `event_id` for a
Teacher-originated request. It contains bounded request/result identities,
Teacher audit references, a localized business notification, and optional
idempotent Dialog delivery identity. It stores no generated curriculum,
mastery, prompt, provider error, or chain-of-thought. Acceptance commits before
Dialog delivery; redelivery reuses the event ID and repairs an interrupted
append without producing a second message.

## `teacher_onboarding_action_receipt`

Migration `016` stores one private receipt per public UUID idempotency key, with
one active `claimed|applied` action per student/general Dialog. It stores only
binding/source/block/action identities, request hash, versions, status,
downstream command/message UUIDs, lease and timestamps—never answers, labels,
option values, profile text, or message bodies.

Migration `018` adds the complete canonical-materialization contract. Every row
has `execution_mode=legacy|canonical`. A canonical claim has a stable required
`canonical_message_command_id`; only `materialized` has a required
`canonical_student_message_id`, cleared lease, and completion timestamp. The
partial unique key `(dialog_id, source_message_id, source_message_version,
block_id, action_id)` prevents two canonical receipts for the same frozen UI
action. Legacy `claimed|applied|completed|rejected` shapes remain valid and
unchanged. Rollback fails closed once canonical mode, either canonical identity,
or `materialized` has been used, then restores the migration-016 constraints.

## Unified onboarding coordinator ledger

Migration `019` adds `teacher_onboarding_interaction` and
`teacher_onboarding_turn` plus coordinator staging fields on
`teacher_dialog_job`. One Dialog has at most one active/reserved frozen prompt
interaction. One turn is bound to the exact Teacher job/source event and stable
Student/response command UUIDs. It may retain only one causal or fallback AI
execution and a digest-bound selected semantic command/confirmation projection;
provider envelopes, prompt variables, model bodies, unselected candidates, and
the user-visible reply are excluded. The visible reply stays only in the
existing private job delivery field until normal Dialog append. This migration
is additive and remains dark by default.

Migration `020` adds an immutable `closed` interaction state with exact reason
`planning_ready|active_path_exists` and `closed_at`. It lets terminal ensure
invalidate an unreserved prompt without a fake successor, job, receipt, UI, or
body marker. Active prompt replacement, terminal close, and new canonical
receipt claim use a per-Dialog transactional fence. A reserved or action-claimed
prompt is never stolen. Down migration requires a drain and is fail-closed when
close evidence or a canonical `claimed|applied|materialized` prompt-effect
receipt exists.

For an accepted policy-v2 Student effect, the existing turn remains
`student_staged` during exact-receipt recovery and the Planner read. Product
response body/UI, job `delivery_pending`, and turn `delivery_pending` then
commit together. Planner reason/path/graph data is not persisted.

## Durable onboarding Planner handoff

Migration `021` adds `teacher_onboarding_plan_handoff`, a bounded Teacher-owned
command/outbox and notification checkpoint. Its exact natural fence is
`(student_id, state_ref_kind, state_ref_version)`; a different goal cannot
create a second local intent for the same authoritative snapshot. Stable UUIDs
and an immutable request hash bind Planner dispatch and deterministic Dialog
notification retries. The only business projection is the supported goal
identity and locale. Student profile, raw model/message bodies, opaque graph
payload, and course/path/lesson identities are forbidden.

The lifecycle is `queued -> dispatching -> accepted -> message_pending ->
delivered`, with `active_path` and `blocked` alternatives. Planner acceptance
persists its handoff ID and canonical `readiness_observed_at`, but means only a
historical non-executable admission: execution is `NOT_STARTED` and content is
`NOT_CREATED`. An S5-origin enqueue atomically changes the reserved prompt to
`handoff_pending` and releases the source job without advancing its dense
cursor. After the one idempotent Dialog notification is proven, ledger,
interaction, turn, job, outcome, and cursor complete in one transaction.

Planner acknowledgement (`planner_handoff_id`, `accepted_at`, and
`readiness_observed_at`) and Dialog delivery acknowledgement
(`notification_message_id` and `delivered_at`) are write-once database
evidence. They may transition together from absent to present exactly once;
they can never be cleared or replaced. The database also permits only the
documented lifecycle transitions, while lease, retry and error fields remain
mutable within those transitions.

Both Planner and Dialog ambiguous acknowledgements replay exact stable command
keys. Expired leases are reclaimable; malformed/semantic conflicts block and
5xx/timeouts retry. The down migration starts an explicit transaction, takes
`ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` locks on the ledger and interaction table, and fails closed
permanently after any ledger row or `handoff_pending` interaction exists. It is
valid only for an unused empty installation. To roll back service behaviour,
operators disable new S8 admissions and drain the worker while retaining all
immutable ledger evidence; there is no destructive cleanup path.

Migration `022` adds the default-dark `teacher_onboarding_path_outcome_inbox`.
It accepts one strict Planner outcome per `execution_id`, fences it to the
immutable S8 `planner_handoff_id`, and stores only the exact Student/Dialog/
Teacher identities, bounded status-specific path IDs, localized message body,
and idempotent Dialog delivery checkpoint. `PATH_READY` requires course,
learning-path, and first-lesson UUIDs; `ACTIVE_PATH_EXISTS` and
`STATE_CHANGED` forbid them. No Planner graph/profile/provider/error or browser
metadata is stored. Acceptance precedes Dialog append and replay reuses the
event ID. The down migration refuses to remove retained outcome evidence.

## Canonical onboarding session cutover

Migration `023` is installed only during a quiesced deployment; S10 and S11
writers must never coexist after it commits. Before changing the schema it
independently rejects every nonterminal interaction, onboarding turn (including
text turns with no interaction link), onboarding coordinator job (including a
job with no turn), and `claimed|applied` receipt. Existing terminal interaction
rows are not assigned a guessed version.

Every new interaction then requires immutable `session_schema_version=1|2|3`.
S11 admits only version 3, while recovery keeps the exact stored version. The
narrow `teacher_onboarding_terminal_session` table records only direct
`ACTIVE_PATH_EXISTS` recovery evidence: deterministic identity, exact
Student/Teacher/Dialog and Student state reference, schema version 3, stable
Dialog command, and `message_pending|delivered` acknowledgement. It contains
no message body, answers, goal, graph, course, path, lesson, or AI data. The
pending row commits before Dialog append; exact concurrent retries reuse the
command and acknowledgement. Causal identity is immutable, and delete and
truncate are rejected. Down migration refuses any stamped interaction or
terminal row, so operational rollback keeps migration 023 and disables only
new admission after draining writers.

Migrations are paired, ordered SQL files under `db/migrations`. Migration `002` drops the outbox before the referenced decision table during rollback. Migration `004` adds the action link and inbox; its task-correlation checks are `NOT VALID` so legacy rows do not block upgrade while new rows are enforced. Migration `005` adds the private teacher-dialog job table, `006` adds per-student souls, and `007` adds pedagogy audit metadata. Migration `008` requeues only untouched general jobs previously blocked as unsupported. Migration `009` does the same for lesson jobs after Dialog has gained revision/selection anchors. Migration `010` adds the intervention inbox, `011` adds Telegram links/bindings/delivery, `012` persists the source channel on durable Dialog jobs, `013` adds the idempotent Learning Planner outcome inbox, and published migrations `014`–`016` remain prerequisites. Checkpoint migrations `017`, `018`, and `019` then add dense v2 turn ordering, canonical action materialization, and the default-dark unified onboarding coordinator respectively. Migration `020` adds S7 terminal interaction closure, migration `021` adds the default-dark S8 handoff ledger, migration `022` adds the default-dark S9 Planner outcome inbox, and migration `023` enforces the canonical session-version cutover and direct active-path terminal ledger. Any unrelated unpublished local migration must use the next available number in its own patch.
